column1: # Per-file TIMEOUT ALLOWANCE registry for tools/cpan-scoreboard.pl (the CPAN
# board).  Same shape and same rules as baselines/perl-suite-timeouts.tsv, read
# The effective per-file timeout is max(seconds, --timeout).  Registering a
# file is NOT a skip and NOT an excuse: it still runs, still reports, still
# counts its failures.  What it buys is that the file is measured AT ALL — the
# board's FAIL rule is "zero ok", so a file killed on the clock is recorded
# `FAIL 0 0 124` and every one of its passing rows vanishes with nothing
# saying so.  That is the #176 pack.t lesson, and the board had no answer to it
# NOT FOR HANGS: this registry promises "give the file the time and it
# finishes".  A file that returns the SAME rows at 10x the budget is stuck, not
# slow, and belongs in a task with its profile instead.
# Rules: one line per file WITH A CAUSE naming the measurement it was sized
# from; size it from a measured run and round up ~1.5x for machine load; when a
# file gets faster, DELETE its row.

column3: s473w/#1512: measured 150 s wall under PCL (perl 0.2 s) and it RUNS TO COMPLETION — at the 120 s default the board recorded FAIL 0/0 rc 124 and the file's rows were invisible.  Sized from the 150 s measurement + the 260 s the profiled run needed under sb-sprof, rounded up.
